identity.real_world_identity_notes: Chevrolet and Corvette Racing specify the Z06 GT3.R with a six-speed sequential motorsport transaxle. The base AMS2 telemetry identity was live-tested; the exact Low Downforce identity is treated as an aero-package alias inheriting the base controls and has not been separately live-tested.

wheel_rim.notes: Direct AMS2 cockpit inspection showed an open-top GT/Formula rim without an integrated display; exact diameter remains unknown.

notes: With Auto Clutch disabled, AMS2 1.6.9.91 moved the base car from rest without physical clutch input. The underlying simulator mechanism was not established.
All six forward gears were selected by paddles, and clutch-free full-throttle upshifts were accepted with a perceptible automatic cut.
Clutch-free downshifts were accepted with the driver's foot off the throttle, and automatic blip was directly visible as a throttle-display spike.

The exact Chevrolet Corvette Z06 GT3.R - Low Downforce identity is approved as an aero-package alias inheriting these controls. Only the base identity was live-tested; the Low Downforce configuration remains an explicit assumption to revisit if contrary behavior is observed.

identities.value: Chevrolet Corvette Z06 GT3.R - Low Downforce

notes: The base identity was live-tested in AMS2 1.6.9.91 with Auto Clutch disabled.

Clutch-free move-off, six paddle-selected gears, no-lift clutch-free upshifts with automatic cut, clutch-free downshifts with automatic blip, and an open-top no-display GT/Formula rim were directly observed.
The exact Low Downforce identity inherits the tested base controls as an approved aero-package assumption; that configuration was not separately live-tested.

confidence.basis: The base exact identity and complete user-facing control technique were directly checked in AMS2; manufacturer sources independently establish the six-speed sequential hardware. The Low Downforce alias is a separately disclosed aero-package assumption.

claims.basis: Official addition plus the exact live telemetry name and GT3_Gen2 class observed through SimHub 9.11.22.

The Low Downforce name is an exact observed SimHub identity. Its controls are explicitly inherited from the live-tested base car as an aero-package assumption; the variant itself has not been live-tested.
Manufacturer sources specify a six-speed sequential motorsport transaxle, while direct cockpit testing established paddle actuation and exercised all six forward gears.
Direct base-car testing established clutch-free move-off, no-lift clutch-free upshifts with perceptible cut, and clutch-free downshifts with a visible automatic-blip spike.
Direct cockpit inspection showed an open-top GT/Formula rim without an integrated display, consistent with the official wheel reference imagery.

notes: Low Downforce is an exact approved alias whose controls are inherited from the verified base car; it has not been separately live-tested.

The wheel-rim shape was originally recorded as "gt-style". The separate "gt-style", "formula" and "prototype" values described the same rim: molded grips at 9 and 3 with a control face between them, usually carrying a display and rev lights. They are merged into "gt-formula". The rim was not observed again and nothing about the observation changed.
